intended_object: The derived series of a Lie algebra L over a commutative ring R: L^(0) = L and L^(k+1) = [L^(k), L^(k)], with every term an ideal of L. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation on solvable Lie algebras.
explanation: The k-th term is `derivedSeriesOfIdeal R L k ⊤`, which applies the map I ↦ ⁅I, I⁆ k times to the ideal ⊤ = L. Here ⁅I, I⁆ is the ideal bracket, i.e. the Lie ideal spanned by all brackets ⁅x, y⁆ with x, y in I. So term 0 is L and term k+1 is [L^(k), L^(k)], which is exactly the textbook derived series. Taking the terms as ideals of L is standard. The setting, a Lie algebra over a commutative ring, is the usual general one: the definition only needs a Lie algebra structure, and Mathlib has no more general version of this notion. The iterate starts at ⊤, so no degenerate case (k = 0, the zero Lie algebra) goes wrong.
